contract: GET /auth/openid/callback. Validate callback state, issuer, signature, audience, nonce and provider errors before matching/creating an allowed user; preserve web cookies/native redirect and group-derived permission semantics; consume callback state once.

invariants.contract: A web callback with a valid provider answer answers 302 to the auth_cb URL with setToken=<the user's legacy token>&accessToken=<JWT> and no state parameter; it sets an HttpOnly Path=/ refresh_token cookie and a Secure SameSite=Strict openid_id_token cookie, links authOpenIDSub on exactly one new active 'user' whose username/email come from the userinfo, creates exactly one session whose refreshToken is the cookie value, and the access token (claims userId, username, type=access, future exp) authenticates GET /api/me as that user with hasOpenIDLink true.
exceptions: auth_state is never set on a web start (a state query makes the web start fail), so the success redirect cannot contain &state; the absence is asserted.

invariants.contract: A web callback whose ID token has a broken RS256 signature, a foreign issuer, a foreign audience or an expired exp answers 302 /login?error=Unauthorized&autoLaunch=0; a provider error=access_denied or a mismatched state answers the same Unauthorized redirect; a token endpoint rejection (invalid_grant) answers 302 /login?error=Error in callback&autoLaunch=0. Each rejection creates no user or session and consumes the flow.
exceptions: The error strings are asserted because the web client reads login?error= and shows it; the HTML of the login page is free.

invariants.contract: Replaying a consumed web callback with the same session and auth cookies answers 302 to /login?error=No sign-in session&autoLaunch=0 and creates no additional user or session.

The native callback with the app's code_verifier answers 200 with the login payload: user id/username/type=user/isActive/hasOpenIDLink, non-empty accessToken, refreshToken and legacy token, default permissions (download and accessAllLibraries true), Source=docker, a non-null userDefaultLibraryId equal to the first-displayOrder library, serverSettings.version/language and an ereaderDevices array. The provider token request carried grant_type=authorization_code, the code, redirect_uri=<origin>/auth/openid/mobile-redirect and that verifier; exactly one session row holds the returned refresh token and it refreshes.
exceptions: The token request form is observed at the stubbed provider; it is not part of the client protocol but proves the verifier was forwarded.

invariants.contract: Repeating the native token-exchange callback with its consumed session answers 400 with body 'No session' and creates no second user or session; the route rejects before any provider token request.

Without a browser session, a callback with no code_verifier or an empty code_verifier is treated as web and answers 302 /login?error=No sign-in session&autoLaunch=0; a non-empty code_verifier, a repeated code_verifier parameter (array) or the auth_method=openid-mobile cookie answers 400 with body 'No session'. None creates a user or session.
exceptions: This pins the upstream truthiness decision for code_verifier because the official app always sends one on the native callback and the web client never sends one.

invariants.contract: A started web flow still completes after the same browser makes other requests with its session cookie; the flow is not bound to the start request. The Express session store keeps sessions for 24 hours of inactivity; the exact boundary is not exercised.
exceptions: The 24-hour boundary and rolling session-touch renewal are not executable within a bounded run; only survival across other requests is asserted.

invariants.contract: When the user linked to the subject is deactivated after a flow starts, the callback answers 302 /login?error=Unauthorized&autoLaunch=0, creates no session for that user and leaves the user row (including its updatedAt) unchanged.

exceptions: force is not applicable: GET /auth/openid/callback has no force, override or refresh mode.

Nonce binding is not executable against the pinned strategy: with response_type=code it sends no nonce and validates none, so the invalid-token scenarios cover signature, issuer, audience and exp instead.
Mapping note: named internal Go tests are assertion leads only; the shared scenarios are the executable oracle.
